outliers.title: She Survived the Titanic… and Two More Ship Disasters 😳
outliers.description:
Violet Jessop survived the Titanic, and it wasn't even her first disaster at sea. In 1911 she was a stewardess on the Olympic when a navy warship rammed it. In 1912 she escaped the Titanic in lifeboat 16, holding a baby an officer handed her. Then in 1916 she was a nurse on the hospital ship Britannic when it hit a mine and sank in under an hour. She jumped from her lifeboat, hit her head on the ship, and still survived.

outliers.title: She Survived the Titanic, but Wasn't Her Last Shipwreck
outliers.description: Violet Jessop went to sea as a stewardess at 21 to support her family, and she survived three disasters on three sister ships. In September 1911 she was working on the Olympic when the cruiser HMS Hawke rammed it and tore a hole in its side; nobody died. Seven months later she moved to the Titanic, and on 14 April 1912 it hit an iceberg while she was asleep. She was put in lifeboat 16 and picked up by the Carpathia the next morning. outliers.title: This Could Be the Worst Ebola Outbreak in History: Doctor Explains
outliers.description:
The 2026 Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has become the largest ever recorded in the country’s history, driven by the uncommon Bundibugyo strain. While international aid and local treatment capacity have scaled up significantly over the past four months, the virus continues to outpace the response as it shifts into new provinces.

outliers.title: Titanic vs Britannic vs Lusitania: Which One Sank Fastest? 🕯️
outliers.description:
Three of the most famous ocean liners ever built, and three very different sinkings:

Lusitania: torpedoed at 2:10 pm on 7 May 1915, about 11 nautical miles off the Old Head of Kinsale, Ireland. She sank in 18 minutes. 1,197 people were lost.

Britannic: Titanic's younger sister, serving as a hospital ship. She struck a mine at 8:12 am on 21 November 1916 in the Aegean Sea and sank in 55 minutes. 30 of the 1,066 people on board were lost. outliers.title: Titanic vs Britannic vs Olympic: Only One Survived 🕯️
outliers.description:
Titanic, Britannic and Olympic were the three Olympic-class sisters, built by Harland & Wolff in Belfast.

Britannic: serving as a hospital ship, she struck a mine at 8:12 am on 21 November 1916 in the Aegean Sea and sank 55 minutes later. 30 of the 1,066 people on board were lost.

Titanic: struck an iceberg at 11:40 pm on 14 April 1912 and sank at 2:20 am, 2 hours and 40 minutes later. More than 1,500 people were lost.

outliers.title: The 2026 Ebola Outbreak Is Still Spreading — Doctor Reacts
outliers.description:
Why is Ebola so difficult to stop? In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the virus continues to spread into new communities where the outbreak response hasn't caught up yet. 

Bundibugyo Ebola is killing approximately one half of the people it infects. But stopping it takes much more than treatment centers. It requires trained doctors and nurses, functioning laboratories, contact tracing, case finding, safe burial, community education—an entire public health system working together.
